title: One Hidden Meta Muse Setting Could Let Attackers Turn the AI Assistant Into a Backdoor
summary: Malware already running on a Mac can quietly take over Meta's Muse assistant and use the broad access its owner granted the app, security researcher Patrick Wardle has shown in a proof-of-concept released on September 21.
card_summary: Malware already running on a Mac can quietly take over Meta's Muse assistant and use the broad access its owner granted the app, security researcher Patrick Wardle has shown in a proof-of-concept released on September 21.

sections.impact:
It works by changing a hidden setting so that when the user taps the microphone and dictates a prompt, the words go to the attacker instead of Meta.

Assessed severity: HIGH.

email_summary: Malware already running on a Mac can quietly take over Meta's Muse assistant and use the broad access its owner granted the app, security researcher Patrick Wardle has shown in a proof-of-concept released on September 21. Severity is rated high.

title: WordPress Comment2Shell Flaw Can Turn Anonymous Comment XSS Into RCE via Admin Session
summary: A new flaw in WordPress core let an anonymous visitor leave a comment that planted a hidden script on the page. If a logged-in administrator later opened that page, the script could run code on the site's server.
card_summary: A new flaw in WordPress core let an anonymous visitor leave a comment that planted a hidden script on the page. If a logged-in administrator later opened that page, the script could run code on the site's server.

sections.technical:
WordPress fixed the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-93485 and dubbed "Comment2Shell," on September 17 in version 7.1.1 and told site owners to update right away. A new flaw in WordPress core let an anonymous visitor leave a comment that planted a hidden script on the page.

Referenced vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-93485.

email_summary: A new flaw in WordPress core let an anonymous visitor leave a comment that planted a hidden script on the page. Tracked as CVE-2026-93485.

title: Zyxel and Veeam Flaws Under Active Exploitation With Command and SYSTEM Access
summary: The U.S. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) on Monday added a now-patched security flaw impacting Zyxel GS1900 series switches to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) catalog, citing evidence of active exploitation.
